answer: fleet-pulse timing notarization: every registration and task reply carries a signed pulse notarized at a rotating beacon quorum — ships logging departure from a wharf, docking at a jetty, reporting position at the horizon. One operator cannot keep hundreds of clones pulsing from distinct hardware clocks: two pulse streams aligning within clock-drift tolerance are declared one vessel, their bond is burned, and a slice funds the audits that caught them. Each fake identity costs real hardware plus a burnable bond.
